new_title: 'Pat at his best': Cats skipper praised after elimination final win

live
AFL elimination final: Geelong vs Carlton live updates - blog, scores and stats
Geelong and Carlton face off in a sudden death elimination final at the MCG as they look to keep their post-season hopes alive.
Follow the live blog below, keep up to date with all the latest stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Geelong vs Carlton live scoreboard
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
Key Event
HT: Carlton 5.7 (37) leads Geelong 5.4 (34)
Three consecutive goals in that second quarter have pulled the game right back for Geelong, who were second best for long stretches of the opening half. But that's where experience tells, because the Cats didn't panic.
They made some adjustments with the way they went forward, stepped up around the clearances and did a better job of closing down the Carlton kick-mark ball movement.
A lot of the key stats really leveled up in that second term. The Blues will not be concerned, they are going to continue to throw everything at this, come what may. But we've got a game on our hands now.
Max Holmes pulls the Cats within three points!
Really hard running from Holmes from the far wing, which was rewarded by a clever Dangerfield kick into his path.
Hasn't been a busy return for Holmes so far, but that is a big goal for the Cats. On the stroke of half-time, they are all the way back in this game.
Brad Close makes it two in a row for the Cats
That's more like it for Geelong. A repeat entry from a Stewart intercept it was, Wiltshire spotting up the lead of Close with a nice kick inside 50. First time they haven't just bombed it on Neale's head.
Again, this is happening with Harry Dean off. The margin is eight points with nine minutes to play in the second quarter.
Gryan Miers pulls one back for the Cats
The Carlton defence does look a little light on without Dean out there, and this time a long ball inside 50 was well brought to ground by Dangerfield. The crumbers went to work and and Miers finished the job with a tidy snap.
The Cats just need to stay close. For now they are achieving that.
Ollie Hollands extends the Carlton lead
Frankie Evans is playing some sort of game. His kicking inside 50 has been spectacular, and that piercing pass to Hollands was the best of the lot.
Carlton get the first of the second, the lead is 21 points and they are looking comfortably the better team. This is powerful stuff from the Blues.
Still no goals in the second quarter
We've got 13 minutes to play in the term, but the rain and the pressure is making for a scrappy affair.
The Blues have missed a couple of chances, but it's been a heavily contested term so far. First goal here will feel pivotal.
Concussion concerns for Harry Dean
The young Carlton defender attempted mark of the century on the wing there, but seems to have smashed his head on something on the way down. He's bleeding heavily out of his nose and looks wobbly on his feet.
No doubt a HIA is on its way. Would be a huge loss if it's serious.
Key Event
QT: Carlton 4.3 (27) leads Geelong 1.5 (11)
Carlton leads the tackle count 19-7, the overall disposal count 96-65 and the clearance count 11-4. They're winning more of the ball, supplying far more pressure and winning it at the coalface.
It's everything Josh Fraser will have wanted to see. If anything the margin flatters the Cats, who have looked a step off the pace so far. Room for improvement for Geelong, but it feels like something is brewing with this Carlton side.
Cooper Lord kicks another for Carlton!
Moments ago it looked like the Cats were going to get away with a really poor first term. Not now.
Carlton's clearance domination earns them another shot on goal straight from the centre bounce, with Lord found inside 50 directly in front.
Patrick Cripps with a stunner! A brilliant captain's goal!
We probably won't see a better goal than that one tonight! Patty Cripps, stuck deep in the pocket and handed a rushed handball from Sam Walsh, has let rip with a checkside from the boundary line that has split the middle post-high.
The Blues are still riding the good feelings, and when Cripps is pulling those off, anything is possible.
Patrick Dangerfield! He finds Geelong's first
Thought he's looked a step slow so far tonight, but not that time. Danger found a pocket of space out the back of a forward 50 stoppage and snapped a ripper off a step.
The Cats needed that so badly. Incredibly, they only trail by four points.
Another Geelong miss from Shannon Neale
How's he missed that one? After a strong mark 20 from goal, somehow Neale has slid his kick wide to the right. The wait for for the first Geelong goal goes on.
Three minutes to play in the first.
Matt Cottrell slots another for the Blues
Best passage of kick-mark footy of the game so far from the Blues. Really clever stuff from full-back to inside 50, all the way to Cottrell who slots the Blues' second.
They are playing without fear, Carlton, that much is clearly evident. They're dominating the clearances and are using the ball brilliantly at the moment.
Frankie Evans kicks the first goal for the Blues
Outstanding tackling pressure from Evans there, having two pops at Mannagh and nailing him with the second one to win the holding the ball free.
From 45 out, Evans made no mistake. First blood Carlton.
Shocking miss from Blake Acres
Acres won the free kick about 25 out, directly in front, but badly shanked the set shot. Blues are settling well here, biting off aggressive targets and now actually sticking some.
Just need to hit the scoreboard with it.
A couple of behinds each
Ball has mostly live in Geelong's front half as the Blues have struggle to get it out of defence. A few early Carlton fumbles as the temperature rises.
Rain is falling at the MCG. We're five minutes into the first term with no goals.
Key Event
Ready to go at the MCG
After the Welcome to Country, national anthem and an almighty roar this elimination final is about to get underway.
Chris Scott flagged in the pre-game coverage that Carlton's midfield has beaten up Geelong's in recent meetings, so that will be will early attentions are drawn. Superstars on both sides in that centre square. Looks like Oisin Mullin is going to be running with Sam Walsh. And in other news, Jeremy Cameron is playing in defence, or at least he's starting there.
Let's get it on.
A massive MCG reception for both sides
They reckon we're on for about 94,000 at the 'G tonight, which is quite something. The Blues played and prevailed in front of a huge crowd last week, so the atmosphere will feel familiar to them. And pretty much nothing is new for these Cats.
We're not far away from the bounce now, formalities to come before we have lift off.
The San Francisco 49ers are here
They're playing the LA Rams at the MCG next Friday for reasons that will no doubt make more sense to others than it does to I, but I'm sure they'll be impressed by what they see tonight.
new_text:
AFL elimination final: Geelong ends Carlton's fairytale season as five-goal Patrick Dangerfield turns clock back
Geelong has ended Carlton's fairytale season with a solid win, after withstanding an early challenge to run away with their elimination final.
In the first finals meeting of the two teams since the 1995 grand final, Carlton got the early jump but could not keep control, as Geelong secured the win by 33 points on a rainy night at the MCG.
Geelong skipper Patrick Dangerfield led the way with five goals in his 378th AFL game.
Cats coach Chris Scott said Dangerfield stood tall when it counted.
"Late, [Dangerfield] was just so impressive," Scott said.
"It also wasn't as if he was bullying inexperienced players. He looked like Pat at his best."
The loss ended Carlton's season after a monumental run of 12 wins and a draw out of 16 games to get to the elimination final under new permanent coach Josh Fraser.
Geelong will travel to Perth to face Fremantle next week in a cut-throat semifinal.
Look back at how the action unfolded in the live blog below.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Geelong vs Carlton scoreboard
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
That's it for the blog tonight
We'll leave it there! Two finals down this weekend with two more to go, and the blog will be back tomorrow for both Sydney-Brisbane and Adelaide-Western Bulldogs. I hope yo can join us then.
For now, the night belongs to Geelong. On to the next one for Chris Scott and his Cats.
Chris Scott is up now
A bit here from the Geelong coach:
"I thought we were outplayed early in the game. We knew there would be periods where they would have the ascendency, their form has been red hot. Their guys in and around the ball are a real handful for us.
"I know there were a lot of rushed behinds, but there were a lot of scoring shots too. I thought we were dominant after quarter-time.
"It was really challenging when we lost [Max Holmes], but it was also really challenging to make the decision to play him tonight. But we had so much faith in the people that worked with him."
Josh Fraser has been speaking to media
A few bits and pieces here from the Carlton coach:
"We started the game reasonably well, but once their stoppage game and contest stepped up we found it really difficult.
"Tonight was disappointing, and we certainly don't want to be a club that lives in mediocrity. The players deserve a lot of credit, so do the staff and coaching group, but we don't want to be a club that is satisfied with finishing eighth.
"We were outplayed, they were far too good.
"I feel like I've got a really good handle on where we're at and understand we have a lot of work in front of us. We need to build depth, improve our players and build our system."
Match report: Cats kick clear to end Blues' stunning AFL season
Geelong have ended Carlton's dream run, kicking clear in the second half to win their AFL elimination final by 33 points.
Trailing by 21 points in the second term on Friday night, the Cats reduced the margin to three points at the main break and kicked 10 goals to six after halftime for the 14.23 (107) to 11.8 (74).
The crowd of 96,680 was the biggest for an AFL match at the MCG this season.
The Cats will head to Perth next week and play Fremantle in next week's semi-finals.
Geelong captain Patrick Dangerfield kicked five goals in the wet conditions, including three in the final quarter.
Midfielder Shaun Mannagh continued his strong form with 25 possessions and six clearances.
Under new coach Josh Fraser, Carlton turned around their disastrous 1-9 start to the season with a stunning run of 12 wins, two losses and a draw before Friday night's season-ending loss.
AAP
Patrick Dangerfield's night out
Let's go through the statline, shall we? And keep in mind Danger played exclusively forward tonight, no midfield time at all.
21 disposals. Five goals. 10 score involvements. 10 contested possessions. Two clearances. 485 metres gained.
Now there was a little bit of junk time in that, but it's also true that Dangerfield looked Geelong's most dangerous forward all night. He got his rewards in the last for a night of massive effort.
Patrick Cripps reflects on Carlton's night and incredible season
Really does feel like just the beginning for the Blues. Patrick Cripps I'm sure agrees.
Patrick Dangerfield reflects on a standout night
It wasn't perfect, he says, but it was still mighty impressive.
And as the man himself says, Patrick Dangerfield has still got it.
Key Event
FT: Geelong 14. 23 (107) def Carlton 11.8 (74)
Geelong was challenged, Geelong was threatened, but Geelong never blinked. The Cats weathered the early Carlton storm and then flexed their muscle in the second half to highlight the difference between a side on the rise and a battle-hardened group of challengers.
Patrick Dangerfield will take the headlines for his five goals, but I thought the big differnce makers were those classy Geelong half-forwards and lesser-light midfielders. Miers, Mannagh, Wiltshire, Close, players of that ilk whose polish and smarts were the difference in the game.
Carlton showed glimpses of the footy that has carried them from the depths of despair to September, but they ran into a powerful unit and in the end ran out of legs. This result will not detract from their season, but hopefully will inspire added hunger over the summer.
The Cats are heading west, and I don't think the Dockers will be excited to see them coming.
Ben Ainsworth gets one now for the Blues
Been a very solid acquisition for Carlton this year, that being his 30th goal of the campaign. A strong return for a small forward.
We've got 3:15 to play in this one, Geelong leads it by 32.
Cooper Lord dribbles another through for the Blues
These are consolation goals for Carlton at this point, but Lord won't turn down his second.
When things have gone well for Carlton, that forward line has ended up very open. Hasn't been enough of it in this second half.
Bailey Smith! A bomb from 50... which is touched
Bailey just set that one up on the breeze and let it float its way on through. It's all going Geelong's way in this second half.
Not been Smith's best night, but he's certainly done his bit.
EDIT: Never mind, the ARC says Jagga Smith touched it. Ahh well.
Brodie Kemp pulls one back for the Blues
The sting has long since gone out of the game as the rain tips down, but the Blues this time are able to find enough numbers out the back for Kemp to goal from the line.
Seven minutes still to play in this last quarter and it looks like Chris Scott is taking the veterans off the ground. They've got a trip to Perth to prepare for.
Patrick Dangerfield has five goals in a final!
He's going ballistic! Danger initially dropped the mark from the Holmes kick, but his new opponent Jacob Weitering went to ground and left the Cats skipper a free run at it.
Dangerfield gathered, stepped, and bombed one home off a step from 50. It's a remarkable night for a champion footballer.
Frankie Evans grabs another for the Blues
He's been one of Carlton's best tonight and one of their real success stories of 2026. He stuck the tackle on Blicavs, was rewarded with the HTB call and nailed his second.
The crowd is thinning, but the Blues faithful who have remained will be pleased to see yet another Evans goal.
Make it four for Patrick Dangerfield!
So of his last three finals, he was best on ground in the 2025 prelim, totally anonymous in the 2025 granny, and now among the best on ground in the 2026 elimination final.
A pretty soft high free kick earned him another look at the big sticks, and Danger made no mistake. The Cats might start thinking about resting some players now.
Patrick Dangerfield has three! The Cats are surely home
He's still got it, Danger. He's been Geelong's most dangerous forward tonight, selfless at times and punishing at others. We've seen him take a loose ball, get around onto that right foot and snap a goal a million times before.
It's a six-goal lead and the Cats have kicked seven in a row. It looks like the Carlton fairytale ends here.
Shannon Neale plucks and goals for the Cats!
You don't want to call it this early, but it's going to be mighty tough for the Blues now.
How did Geelong escape Carlton tight on the boundary line? Poor missed tackles, half-hearted defensive efforts. And suddenly Bailey Smith is flowing forward and finding Neale, who did brilliantly to outpoint Weitering. It's 29 now, and nearly done for the Cats.
Final quarter is underway
For one of these sides, this is the final quarter of their season. The Blues need a four-goal turnaround to make sure it's not them.
Ball is in the air, here we go.
Key Event
3QT: Geelong 10.13 (73) leads Carlton 7.8 (50)
That was a powerful quarter from Geelong. They suckered the Blues into their game of Russian roulette and soundly beat them, putting a gap in the game almost entirely off Carlton turnovers.
What now seems stark is that when Carlton was well on top early in the game, Geelong held its nerve and did not get put away. The Blues have not had that same composure during the Cats' strong periods.
Still plenty of time left, but it's all trending one way. Only potential bad news for Geelong is Max Holmes limping from the field at the end of that quarter.
